page: The Microsoft Azure EC4as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance lacks bundled local storage and requires external storage attachments, though it supports Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a pronounced distinction between single-threaded and parallel compute throughput. The instance delivers average single-core performance, scoring 2055.15 in stress-ng and 1183.0 in Geekbench single-core tests. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks land in the lower quartile, reflecting the constraints of its two physical cores; Geekbench multi-core registers at 2516.0, stress-ng multi-core achieves 4309.78, and the PassMark CPU score totals 4754.49. In synthetic database and memory-bound operations, PassMark memory performance reaches an average score of 1879.85, while Redis SET throughput achieves 3.42 million operations per second.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the EC4as_v5 provides high memory density per compute unit without the overhead of enterprise GPU or local NVMe storage attachments. The principal tradeoff is moderate raw compute throughput, making the instance less practical for parallel compile tasks or dense CPU calculations. The system is suited for memory-bound services requiring generous RAM allocations, such as Redis or Memcached instances, relational database replicas relying on remote persistent disks, and medium-scale backend analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure EC4as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, backed by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring 2 physical cores running 2 threads per core, it offers 32 MB of L3 cache and an 8.0 GB per-vCPU memory allocation. The instance includes no local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-thread compute capabilities alongside lower-tier multi-threaded and database scores, reflecting its 2-core hardware envelope. PassMark memory testing registers in the average bracket, and Redis achieves 3.42 million SET operations per second. The EC4as_v5 offers resource efficiency for RAM-heavy workloads with moderate processing demands, fitting distributed caches, in-memory datastores, and mid-tier enterprise business applications.
